about: THE CHAIN saga_rhine_frisia (Design/content/CHAINS.md; the page is Design/content/chains/saga_rhine_frisia.md): THE LAW THAT WAS ONLY SAID. The saga of the Rhine and Frisia: how the law of the Frisians, which lived in the heads of a few wise men on the terps, came to be written for the emperor in 802, and what a merchant who carries the wise men can make of it. Lots are laid on the altar at Doccinga over a man killed in a crowd; a word is carried to Saxmund beyond the Lauwers, whose sister's sons have lost their father's land for the rising of 793; the three lands reckon a man's worth on the terp at Winaldum; the old man of the west says his law at Medemelacha; the emperor's messengers ask at Dorestad who knows the Frisians' law; the wise men go south in the player's boat by Saint Martin's at Traiectum to the palace at Noviomagus; and there the player stands between the wise men and the clerk's pen. Fourteen cards (all harbour), four endings: ch_saga_rhine_frisia_end_draft (what happened: the law is written as it was said, old gods and all, and never finished), ch_saga_rhine_frisia_end_king (changed_lex_frisionum_finished: one clean king's law), ch_saga_rhine_frisia_end_land (changed_frisian_inheritance_802: the right of inheritance comes back twelve years early), ch_saga_rhine_frisia_end_unwritten (changed_lex_frisionum_unwritten: the wise men go home and nothing is written). A last card in 814 is the true end of the inheritance (Louis the Pious gives it back) for every house that did not win it in 802. Real people: Wlemar and Saxmund, the two wise men named in the Additio sapientum of the Lex Frisionum, of whom nothing else is known: where they lived and how they spoke is invented (?). Bernlef (cast.bernlef) and the bishop (cast.hamacar) are spoken of, not met. Everyone else is an ordinary invented person whom the forge names. Progress: flags ch_saga_rhine_frisia_1 to _9; the roads from the hearing are ch_saga_rhine_frisia_road_draft, _road_king, _road_land, _road_unwritten. Waits are flags that lapse (ch_saga_rhine_frisia_wait 20 to 30 days, _hear_wait 3 to 12, _end_wait 60) and the years themselves: nothing can be written before 802. Every chain card after the first has a high weight and a 'when' that asks for the last flag, so it comes on the first call at its port. Every option's 'note' names its outcome text (chain_saga_rhine_frisia.<card>.out_<option>), which the engine does not show yet. Lasting costs: ch_saga_rhine_frisia_cold_terps (the east remembers who helped the pen), ch_saga_rhine_frisia_missi_remember (the palace remembers who lost it a law). Words: Data/writing/chain_saga_rhine_frisia.json. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start: Doccinga, 794 to 801. A man killed in a crowd and nobody knows the hand: Lex Frisionum tit. XIV (up to seven may be named; each swears with eleven; two twigs wrapped in clean wool on the altar or on relics, one cut with a cross; a priest or an innocent boy draws; if the bare twig comes each cuts his own mark and they are drawn until one is left): dossiers/doccinga.md 72, lore/law_tolls.md 5.3 and 6.2, the text by K. Nieuwenhuijsen at keesn.nl/lex (read by the dossier writers; from their notes here). The killing, the wool sale and the seven are invented; Aalsum is a real terp by Dokkum. Wlemar is one of the two wise men of the Additio sapientum; that he said the law at Doccinga and Winaldum is invented (?). The steersman is cast.crew.aldger or a steersman of the forge. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_1 and _swore, _bought_out or neither; _wait runs 20 days.

cards.note: Step 2: Emuthon, after step 1, before 806. Saxmund is the other wise man of the Additio sapientum ('Haec iudicia Saxmundus dictavit'); that he is of the land between Lauwers and Weser is invented (?), though the judgement on the shrine-breaker that follows his is marked 'beyond the Lauwers'. The lost inheritance is true: Louis the Pious in 814 'restored to the Saxons and Frisians the right of their fathers' inheritance, which under his father they had lawfully lost for their faithlessness' (the Astronomer, Vita Hludowici c. 24; our rendering); the rising east of the Lauwers is Altfrid, Vita Liudgeri I.22, and the defeat on the Weser in Rustringen is Annales regni Francorum 793. The widow and her sons are invented. The wergild of 106 solidi and 2 pennies and the solidus of two pennies east of the Lauwers: Lex Fris. I and the money clauses, as in dossiers/emuthon.md 47 and 81 (?). Black quernstones of Mayen lava reached every terp (economy/stone_metal_arms.md). Bernlef's line needs the spine's flag ms_bernlef_met. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_2 and _carried_sax or _querns; _wait runs 30 days.

cards.note: Step 3: Winaldum, thirty days or more after step 2, before 806. The three lands and their three scales are the Lex Frisionum's own: between Vlie and Lauwers a noble 80 solidi at three pennies the solidus; between Lauwers and Weser 106 solidi and 2 pennies at two; between Sincfal and Vlie 100 at two and a half (Lex Fris. I and the money clauses, as read in dossiers/wijnaldum.md 46, emuthon.md 47 and 81, medemelacha.md 43) (?): 240, 214 and 250 pennies. Charlemagne's heavier penny came in 793/794 (about 1.7 g for about 1.3 g: economy/silver_coin.md); the hunger is Annales Laureshamenses 793. That the wise men met and reckoned with beans, and asked a merchant, is invented. The riddle Wlemar pays with is riddle_exeter_13_ten_chickens (riddles_793.json): a counting riddle, six and four, for a man who has just counted. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_3 and _reckoned or _tilted.

cards.note: Step 5: Dorestad, spring and summer, 802 to 805. The wait is the years themselves. In 802 Charles, emperor since Christmas 800, sent messengers through the realm in pairs, a churchman and a count, strangers to their district (Capitulare missorum generale, MGH Capit. I no. 33), and in October at Aachen 'gathered the dukes, the counts and the rest of the Christian people with the men of law, and had all the laws in his realm read out, and each man's law given to him, and mended wherever it was needed, and the mended law written, and that the judges should judge by what was written and take no gifts' (Annales Laureshamenses 802; our rendering). Einhard c. 29: he had the unwritten laws of all the peoples under him set down. The Lex Saxonum and the Ewa ad Amorem of the IJssel Franks are of the same work (lore/law_tolls.md 5.4). That the Frisians were heard at the palace of Noviomagus on the way is invented: the place of the hearing is not recorded (?). The clerk and the count are invented. Ten shillings are 120 d in the king's reckoning. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_5 and _kings_fee or _told_clerk; _wait runs 20 days.

cards.note: Step 6: Winaldum, twenty days or more after step 5, before 807. The quarrel is the Lex Frisionum's own two faces. The sand the tide covers: Additio sapientum XI, De honore templorum: 'Qui fanum effregerit et ibi aliquid de sacris tulerit, ducitur ad mare, et in sabulo, quod accessus maris operire solet, finduntur aures eius, et castratur, et immolatur diis quorum templa violavit' (the Latin as in dossiers/wijnaldum.md 73 and the spine's sources; the English is ours), set after the words that mark the law beyond the Lauwers. Whether it was still used is not known; most think it an old judgement that was said and not done. Saxmund's refusal is invented and rests on the lost inheritance (step 2). The player's answer is a leaning, not yet a deed: ch_saga_rhine_frisia_lean_all, _lean_clean or _lean_land. Both wise men come aboard for Noviomagus. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_6.

cards.note: Step 7, a side step that opens the hard road: Traiectum, with the wise men aboard, before 807. The way from the Almere to the Rhine is the Vecht, under Saint Martin's (dossiers/traiectum.md, medemelacha.md 11). The Christian clauses the deacon wants said first are the law's own: a man in feud has peace in church, in his house, and on the way to and from church and court (Additio I.1, Wlemar's: 'Homo faidosus pacem habeat in ecclesia, in domo sua, ad ecclesiam eundo, de ecclesia redeundo, ad placitum eundo, de placito redeundo', as chains/house_rival.md quotes it); Sunday work four solidi, twelve beyond the Lauwers (tit. XVIII, as dossiers/doccinga.md 46 reads it (?)). The bishop is cast.hamacar to 806 and is not named. That Utrecht pressed its wishes on the wise men, and that a letter of the bishop carried a plea for the disinherited, is invented; a bishop's letter as the way into a palace is ordinary. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_7 and _bishop_letter or _plea.

cards.note: Step 8: Noviomagus, with the wise men aboard, 802 to 806. The palace above the Waal is Charles's own (Einhard c. 17; he kept Easter there in 804, 806 and 808: Annales regni Francorum; dossiers/noviomagus.md). The Saxons' law and the law of the IJssel Franks were taken down in the same years (Lex Saxonum, Ewa ad Amorem: lore/law_tolls.md 5.4); that their law-men waited here beside the Frisians is invented (?). The doorkeeper's price is ordinary. The step is a real wait: ch_saga_rhine_frisia_hear_wait runs twelve days, five with a letter, three with a gift. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_8.

cards.note: Step 9, the turn of the whole chain: Noviomagus, when the wait of step 8 is over. What is written is what the Lex Frisionum holds: the three lands and their scales (tit. I), the kettle (tit. III), the lots (tit. XIV), the Sunday fine (tit. XVIII), the hand of the harper, the goldsmith and the woman who weaves fresum (Additio II, Wlemar's), the public way on the river that may not be blocked, twelve solidi (Additio VI, Saxmund's), and the sand the tide covers (Additio XI); and above two parts of the additions the heading that these judgements Wlemar said, and these Saxmund (lore/law_tolls.md 5; dossiers/wijnaldum.md 46, 72, 73, 85). That a merchant stood between the wise men and the pen is the game's. Four roads: road_draft (as it was said: what happened), road_king (one clean law: check a little Latin, the bishop's letter, or the leaning of step 6), road_land (the inheritance asked first: check the plea of step 7), road_unwritten (they go home). ch_saga_rhine_frisia_end_wait runs 60 days: the assembly is after harvest and news is as slow as a boat. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_9.

cards.note: Ending 1, what happened: Winaldum, sixty days or more after the hearing. The law of the Frisians was written about 802 as a rough working text: three scales side by side, Christian and heathen judgements together, the wise men's additions under their own names. It was never made into a finished law, and is known only from Herold's print at Basel in 1557, from a book now lost (lore/law_tolls.md 5.1; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lex_Frisionum, read 6 Oct 2026). The emperor's question about the sand, the hearth pennies and the oath-right are invented. Rewards: unlock_title_oathworthy_three_lands (a stranger's oath taken as a landsman's: the worth of oath-helpers is the law's own, tit. I) on every road; unlock_factor_wijnaldum; the hard road (the western law carried whole, the scales reckoned true, nothing told to the clerk behind their backs, no name bought off the list) adds unlock_plot_wijnaldum. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_end_draft and _done.

cards.note: Ending 2, history changed (changed_lex_frisionum_finished): Dorestad, sixty days or more after the hearing. In this telling the emperor has what he asked for at Aachen: one mended law of the Frisians, written fair, one scale in his own pennies, the church's peace at its head and no gods on any beach. What would follow is in the chain page. Rewards: unlock_charter_dorestad (toll freedom at Dorestad was a thing the king gave: Charles freed Saint-Germain-des-Pres of the toll at Dorestad, Quentovic and elsewhere in 779, MGH DD Kar. 1 no. 122 (?)); the hard road (scales reckoned true and the western law carried whole, so the clean law is at least a right one) adds unlock_title_emperors_merchant (merchants under the palace's own protection are in Louis the Pious's praeceptum negotiatorum of 828, Formulae imperiales 37: early here (?)). The cost that lasts: ch_saga_rhine_frisia_cold_terps, unless the silver is sent to the widow. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_end_king and _done.

cards.note: Ending 3, history changed (changed_frisian_inheritance_802): Emuthon, sixty days or more after the hearing. In truth the right of inheritance came back only in 814, by Louis the Pious in the first months of his reign (the Astronomer, Vita Hludowici c. 24); here the emperor gives it at the assembly of 802, with the law. What would follow is in the chain page. The widow's sons and the gifts of the houses that have their land again are invented. Rewards: unlock_plot_emuthon on every road; unlock_factor_emuthon; the hard road (Saxmund carried in your own boat and the western law carried whole, nothing told behind their backs) gives unlock_partner_saxmunds_nephew, a sworn partner with a boat of his own. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_end_land and _done.

cards.note: Ending 4, history changed (changed_lex_frisionum_unwritten): Doccinga, sixty days or more after the hearing, at the altar where the lots lay in step 1. In this telling there is no Lex Frisionum: the emperor's chest at Aachen holds the Saxons' law and the Franks', and for the Frisians a note that they have none they can remember. What would follow is in the chain page. The peace sworn on the altar is modelled on the law's own peace for a man in feud (Additio I.1); that it was given to a stranger is invented. Rewards: unlock_title_peace_of_three_lands on every road; unlock_pilot_lauwers (the Lauwers mouth, a bay still forming about 800: dossiers/doccinga.md 10); the hard road (Saxmund carried, the scales reckoned true, the western law carried whole) gives unlock_heirloom_law_of_three_lands: the house itself is taught the law, and an heir inherits it. The cost that lasts: ch_saga_rhine_frisia_missi_remember. Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_end_unwritten and _done.

cards.note: The last card, twelve years on, for every house that did not win the land in 802: Emuthon, 814 to 821. Charles died at Aachen on 28 January 814. His son Louis in the first months of his reign 'restored to the Saxons and Frisians the right of their fathers' inheritance, which under his father they had lawfully lost for their faithlessness; some called it generosity and others want of foresight' (the Astronomer, Vita Hludowici c. 24; our rendering). The widow's son is invented. A step's reward, and a factor at Emuthon for the house that asked first (the leaning of step 6 or the plea of step 7). Sets ch_saga_rhine_frisia_814.
